# OpenAI Acquires Odessia, an AI Travel Agent, From Sonder's Founder


By OpenTools Team


·


November 11, 2026


OpenAI acquired Odessia, an AI travel agent startup founded by Sonder co‑founder Francis Davidson, the companies announced Monday. Built in five months by eight people using GPT‑5.5 and Codex, Odessia had processed over $60 million in annualized travel bookings before being shut down as part of the deal. The acquisition signals OpenAI's ambition to move beyond simply referring users to Booking.com and Expedia.


## Eight People, Five Months, One Working AI Travel Agent


Odessia was a strikingly lean operation. The startup was built from January to June 2026 by a team of eight in San Francisco with no CTO — relying instead on[GPT-5.5](https://opentools.ai/llms/gpt-55) , Codex, and heavy use of coding agents to achieve what founder Francis Davidson claimed was roughly a 30x reduction in build time, according to a pre-acquisition profile by[Michael Schneider](https://schneida.substack.com/p/why-sequoia-led-odessias-6m-pre-seed) . It raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia Capital and launched publicly on October 14, 2026. The product let users plan and book entire trips — flights, hotels, transport, and activities — through a single conversational interface, without being sent to third-party websites.


## From Sonder's Collapse to an OpenAI Deal


Davidson's path to this deal runs through one of the more dramatic founder stories in travel. He co-founded Sonder, grew it to roughly a thousand employees at a $1 billion valuation by age 26, and took it public via SPAC — a move he later told[Schneider](https://schneida.substack.com/p/why-sequoia-led-odessias-6m-pre-seed) he made “way before I was ready.” Sonder's stock fell roughly 99%, Davidson was pushed out as CEO in June 2025, and the company unraveled. Less than a year after Sonder's collapse, he sold his next company to[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) .


## A Deal With Undisclosed Terms, an Immediate Shutdown


The terms of the acquisition were not disclosed, and multiple outlets including[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/openai-acquires-odessia-travel-startup-created-by-sonder-founder/) and[Skift](https://skift.com/2026/11/10/a-year-after-sonders-collapse-francis-davidson-sells-his-ai-travel-startup-to-openai/) characterized it as an acqui-hire. Odessia's service was shut down immediately. Davidson wrote on LinkedIn that Odessia “achieved” its goal of shipping the best AI travel agent, with “over $60M/year of travel planned over the past summer by tens of thousands of early adopters,”[PhocusWire](https://www.phocuswire.com/news/startups/openai-acquires-ai-travel-agent-odessia) reported.


## Why OpenAI Bought a Travel Startup


The acquisition is about more than travel.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) has 1.2 billion weekly active users on ChatGPT and already has travel booking integrations with Booking.com and Expedia. But Odessia gives OpenAI a end-to-end booking agent that had begun the IATA accreditation process, direct access to hotel inventory, and a founder who ran a lodging company for a decade. “OpenAI didn't acquire Odessia for its revenue,”[Skift](https://skift.com/2026/11/10/a-year-after-sonders-collapse-francis-davidson-sells-his-ai-travel-startup-to-openai/) wrote. “It bought a team that built a working AI travel agent in months.” The market noticed: Expedia shares fell nearly 4%,[Tripadvisor](https://opentools.ai/tools/tripadvisor) dropped more than 3%, and Booking Holdings fell more than 2% on the day of the announcement,[PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/online-travel-agencies-shares-drop-following-openai-acquisition-of-travel-startup-odessia/) reported.


## What This Means for AI Builders


Odessia's arc — 8 people, 5 months,[GPT-5.5](https://opentools.ai/llms/gpt-55) + Codex, $6M in funding, acquired by[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) — is a template for AI-native startups. It validates that frontier labs will acquire rather than build into verticals when they see working AI agents with real transaction volume. The deal also shows that domain expertise (Davidson's decade in lodging) plus AI-first execution speed is a formula the labs will pay for. For builders, the signal is straightforward: vertical AI agents that demonstrate real traction are on a path to acquisition, not just competition.
